standard.title: Door Handles for Mortice Locks — Specification (Second Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, workmanship, finish, and performance-testing for door handles (lever door handles and door knobs) used with mortice locks.
standard.scope: This standard specifies requirements for materials, dimensions, manufacture, workmanship, finish, and performance-testing for door handles (lever door handles and door knobs) used with mortice locks.

version.revision: Second Revision (overhauls testing guidelines, updates material chemistry, and introduces the 6-digit classification coding system)
revision_history: Second Revision (overhauls testing guidelines, updates material chemistry, and introduces the 6-digit classification coding system), 2024

amendments.summary: Modifies marking and labeling clauses: substitutes Clause 8.1 (a) to require the 'Manufacturer’s name or brand name or trade mark' instead of the previous text; substitutes Clause 9.1 (a) to require 'Manufacturer’s name or brand name or trade name'; and deletes Clause 9.1 (b) completely.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Door Fittings (Quality Control) Order', all door handles for mortice locks must conform to IS 4992:2024 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, or sold in India.
requirements: Every certified door handle/knob and its packaging box must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the CM/L licence number.
Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 8.1 (a) is modified to require that each individual door handle be clearly and indelibly marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade mark'.

Under Amendment No. 1 (May 2026), Clause 9.1 (a) is modified to require that each packaging carton be marked with the 'Manufacturer's name or brand name or trade name', while the previous packaging marking requirement under Clause 9.1 (b) is completely deleted.
Covers two main types: a) Lever door handles; b) Door knobs.
Handles must withstand high pulling forces (tested using axial strength apparatus with tension loads up to 1000 N) without stripping threads, breaking, or pulling loose from the spindle.

The spring return mechanism must withstand high durability cyclic testing (up to 200,000 operations depending on durability grade) with zero structural failures, loss of return angle, or spring slippage.
Handles must withstand neutral salt spray testing (up to 240 hours depending on grade) to ensure corrosion resistance on finishes (plated, painted, or anodised layers).
